name: Tosor Pass
near: Tosor village on the south shore of Issyk-Kul (turn-off from the Balykchy — Karakol highway at about km 120 from Balykchy). From the village to the summit of the pass is about 34.7 km of mountain road.
elev: 3893 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, 2GIS, central-asia.guide); dangerousroads.org gives 3901 m, Too.kg — rounded 3900 m. Elevation gain from Tosor village — about 2295 m.
short: A high-altitude off-road pass (3893 m) over the Terskey Ala-Too range — the only road pass on the south shore of Issyk-Kul, leading into Naryn region.
desc: Tosor is a dirt pass over the Terskey Ala-Too range, linking the south shore of Issyk-Kul with the Kichi-Naryn valley and Naryn region. From Tosor village the road climbs 34.7 km up the gorge at an average gradient of 6.6%: at the bottom are sea buckthorn and sandy-stony sections, in the middle deep ruts and narrow spots right by the river, a “stone gate” beyond which the gorge widens, and at the top a stony moraine climb. This is an unmaintained road: it can be driven only in a prepared 4×4, usually in July–September; on the Naryn side there are fords across the Uchemchek River. The gorge and pass are part of the route by which the Kyrgyz fled to China in 1916 during the Urkun; in July 2026 a memorial trek marking the 110th anniversary of the events went along it.
guide: Tosor is not a spot but a whole day on the road: allow all the daylight hours for the Tosor — Naryn crossing (about 11 h according to reviews). If you aren't ready for the pass, drive the lower 5–10 km of the gorge as far as the “stone gate” — sea buckthorn thickets, springs and picnic spots are reachable without assaulting the summit. At the top look at the Terskey glaciers and, on a clear day, at Issyk-Kul behind you; beyond that the road heads toward Jyluu-Suu and the Kichi-Naryn valley. Remember the history: refugees of the Urkun came this way in 1916 — in 2026 a memorial expedition passed here. Don't go with a single car: there is no signal, and the fords on the south side behave differently in the morning and in the afternoon.
see: The Tosor gorge with sea buckthorn thickets and springs in its lower part; the “stone gate” where the gorge turns into a mountain valley; the moraine climb and a panorama of the Terskey Ala-Too glaciers from the 3893 m summit; at the fork at about 3000 m, a turn-off to the neighboring Tamga gorge; on the south side the Uchemchek/Kichi-Naryn valley with its fords, then the Jyluu-Suu hot springs and Lake Teshik-Kol (an alternative approach).
skip: You don't have a prepared 4×4 with an experienced driver and a second vehicle accompanying you. You're going in June or after heavy rain — snow at the top and high water at the fords. What you want is specifically a panorama of Issyk-Kul, not mountain off-roading — for that Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon nearby is easier.
diff: High (for the vehicle and driver): 34.7 km of dirt road, a drop of 2295 m, an average gradient of 6.6%, a stony moraine climb below the summit, fords across the Uchemchek on the south side. For cyclists, long stretches on foot in the upper part. The lower gorge for a walk/picnic is easy.
when: July–September; best August–September, when the snow has gone and the water in the fords is lower (OunTravela). Dangerousroads: usually passable June–August, but snow on the pass can lie until June–July. A late snowfall can close the summit for several days even in season. Closed in winter and spring.
hours: An open area with no barriers or ticket offices; there is no official opening schedule — passability is determined by snow, mudflows and water at the fords. Check conditions with locals in Tosor or with jeep operators before setting out.
daytime: Start the climb early in the morning (6–8 am): the water at the fords is lower in the morning and rises toward evening because of melting; it's best to cross the summit before noon, before afternoon thunderstorms and fog.
how: Balykchy — Karakol highway (south shore) to Tosor village: from Bishkek about 295 km (Bishkek — Balykchy ~175 km + ~120 km along the south shore), 4.5–5 h; from Karakol about 100 km, ~1.5–2 h. In the village turn south into the gorge: the right fork is a mountain road to Bokonbaevo, the short left one goes to the forestry station, straight on leads up to the pass (34.7 km). On the south side, a descent into the Uchemchek/Kichi-Naryn valley and on to Naryn (Tosor — Naryn about 200 km, ~11 h according to a TripAdvisor review).
needcar: Yes — only a prepared 4×4 with high ground clearance, all-terrain tires and a spare, with an experienced driver; best in a convoy of 2+ vehicles (dangerousroads, OunTravela, Too.kg). On foot/by bicycle — a multi-day trek with a tent.
self: Yes, in your own prepared 4×4 and with off-road experience — no permits or fees, and no border zone is mentioned. But going alone (a single car) is not recommended: there is no signal, no fuel stations and no people for tens of km; if you break down it is hard to get out. Beginners — only with a local driver or a jeep tour.
roadtype: Entirely dirt, unmaintained: at the bottom a sandy-stony track, in the middle part deep washouts and ruts, sections right up against the river; below the pass from the north, a stony moraine climb of large rocks. On the south side, several fords across the Uchemchek River with boulders; the water level depends on the time of day and snowmelt (higher in June–July). Conditions change greatly from year to year (OunTravela).
traveltime: Bishkek — Tosor: 4.5–5 h. Karakol — Tosor: ~1.5–2 h. Tosor — summit (34.7 km): 2.5–4 h by 4×4 depending on the condition of the track (estimate from the length and nature of the road). The full Tosor — Naryn crossing: about 11 h (TripAdvisor, ~200 km); central-asia.guide advises allowing the whole daylight day.
stay: There are no guesthouses, cafes or shops in the gorge or on the pass — only a tent (plenty of camping spots and springs, Too.kg). Overnight stays before/after are in the yurt camps and guesthouses of the south shore (Tosor, Tamga, Barskoon, Bokonbaevo): budget options from 500–600 som/person (economist.kg, July 2026). On the Naryn side — guesthouses and CBT Naryn in Naryn.
net: There is no mobile signal in the gorge or on the pass (Too.kg, dangerousroads, central-asia.guide). Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage exists in Tosor village and on the south-shore highway. The participants of the 2026 memorial trek used satellite Starlink. Download offline maps and tracks in advance.
entry: Free: no source from 2016–2026 mentions a transit fee, eco fees or permits (no protected area is noted on the route).
transfer: No published prices for a jeep crossing over Tosor were found — on request only from operators (Ak-Sai, Eurasia Travel, DWC). Reference points for getting there: marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — south shore 500–600 som; taxi 1200 som/person or 4500 som/car (24.kg, July 2026).
bring: A full tank and spare fuel (there are no fuel stations), a spare tire, a compressor, a shovel, a tow rope; warm clothing (at 3900 m there is snow and frost even in summer), a rain jacket, water and purification (livestock in the river — boil the water, Too.kg), a day's food beyond the plan, a first-aid kit, offline maps and a track, and if possible a satellite communicator.
warn: Serious off-roading: a moraine climb, fords with boulders, washouts; don't go without 4×4 experience and a second vehicle. Snow on the pass is possible until July and from late August; after downpours there are mudflows and rockfalls on sections of the road. No signal and no fuel stations. At 3900 m altitude sickness is possible after a fast ascent from lake level (1600 m). River water — only after boiling (livestock graze).
food: There are no establishments on the route — bring food. Before/after, cafes and yurt camps of the south shore: lagman, beshbarmak, kumys in summer; smoked and dried Issyk-Kul fish by the highway. On the 2026 trek, participants cooked traditional kulazyk (Time.kg) — an excellent snack for the road.
reviews: Google Maps (“Tossor Pass”): 5/5, 8 ratings on 03.10.2026. TripAdvisor (Tosor Pass): 4 reviews, 3 “excellent” and 1 “average” (2016–2017; viewed 07.10.2026). Pros: one of the best mountain roads, glaciers and valleys, wild nature, almost no cars. Cons: a very hard stony road, unpredictable weather (snow, fog, hail), a high risk of breakdown far from help.
p.sum: Tosor (≈3893 m) is a serious off-road pass between the south shore of Issyk-Kul and Naryn: from Tosor village it's 34.7 km of rough track to the summit (2.5–4 h), and from the south fords across the Uchemchek and the Kichi-Naryn valley; the whole Tamga — Tosor — Naryn crossing is ≈365 km (90% dirt), a full daylight day. Go only in a prepared 4×4, preferably two vehicles, in August–September (less water at the fords, snow gone). Without your own vehicle — jeep tours (Eurasia Travel, Ak-Sai, DWC). Stay overnight before/after in Tosor, Tamga or Barskoon (guesthouses $12–40, yurt camps $80–90 on Booking); on the pass — a tent only.

p.iti.0.title: Day trip from Tosor/Tamga (without the crossing)
p.iti.0.plan: 8:00 set out in a 4×4 → 10:30–11:30 summit, photos of the glaciers → descend by 15:00 → Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon at sunset.
p.iti.1.title: Crossing Issyk-Kul → Naryn (1–2 days)
p.iti.1.plan: Night in Tosor → 6:30 depart → 10:00 pass → Uchemchek fords by noon → Kichi-Naryn → evening in Naryn (or a night in a tent at Uchemchek). Then Salkyn-Tor, Tash-Rabat, Song-Kol.
p.iti.2.title: What to combine it with
p.iti.2.plan: Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon, Barskoon waterfalls, the Manjyly-Ata valley; in the south — Naryn, Salkyn-Tor, Eki-Naryn.
p.season: January–May: closed by snow. June–mid-July: snow on the summit, peak water at the fords. Late July–September: the best period. October: first snowfalls.
p.budget.economy: The crossing is not possible independently without a 4×4; to Tosor — marshrutka 500–600 som, guesthouse 1000–3000 som ($12–36), a walk in the lower gorge is free.
p.budget.comfort: Jeep tour with the crossing — from $2300 for a 12-day program (Eurasia) or individually on request; lodging $80–90 in Tosor yurt camps.
p.permits: Not needed; there is no border zone or fees.
p.access: Only for experienced 4×4 drivers; hard on children and older people (jolting, 3900 m altitude). The lower gorge is accessible for a family picnic.
